title: Move semantics
summary: Assignment moves ownership. Learn to read E0382 and pick between borrowing, cloning, and restructuring.

steps.note: `a` owns the String. Three words on the stack point at heap text.
The three stack words are copied into `b`. The heap text is not copied, and `a` is no longer usable.
`b` is read through a shared borrow. Nothing moves.
`b` goes out of scope and the heap text is freed exactly once.

examples.caption: The canonical E0382. Predict the error before you run it.
An i32 is Copy, so the same shape compiles and prints both.
Borrowing lets a function read the value without taking it.
Passing by value is an assignment into the parameter, so it moves too.
Cloning is allowed. It is a cost you chose, and it is visible in the code.

references.title: The Rust Programming Language, ch. 4: Understanding Ownership
